description: Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.

b.request: Using only fee records with `rebrate` strictly greater than 0.0005, group by `orderslink` and compute each order's average `rebtotal` and average of `rebrate`/`feerate` (ignoring nulls), then divide each order's average ratio by the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders (only when that mean is not null), and show `orderslink`, average `rebtotal`, average ratio, and relative ratio for the top 10 orders by relative ratio descending with nulls last.
b.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN p.avg_ratio / o.mean_ratio END AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

a.request: Using only fee records whose maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) is greater than 0.0005, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, compute the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, provided that overall mean is not missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Return the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and this relative ratio for the 10 orders with the highest relative ratio, sorted from highest to lowest with missing values last.
a.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL THEN p.avg_ratio / o.mean_ratio ELSE NULL END AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

c.request: For fee records that clear the 0.0005 maker rebate rate (`rebrate`) threshold, group them by order (`orderslink`) and, for each order, work out the average total rebate (`rebtotal`) and the average of rebate rate divided by fee rate (`rebrate` / `feerate`), ignoring missing values. Then take the mean of those per-order average ratios across all orders and, as long as that overall mean isn't missing, divide each order's average ratio by it. Show the order link, the average total rebate, the average ratio and the relative ratio for the top 10 orders by relative ratio, highest first, with missing values last. Only fee records whose maker rebate rate is strictly greater than 0.0005 are included.
c.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate > 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean_ratio FROM per_order) SELECT p.orderslink, p.avg_rebtotal, p.avg_ratio, CASE WHEN o.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL AND o.mean_ratio <> 0 THEN p.avg_ratio / o.mean_ratio ELSE NULL END AS relative_ratio FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
